newsitem.title: UK: Premier Farnell sells unit to Arrow.
newsitem.headline: Premier Farnell sells unit to Arrow.

text.p: British electronics components and equipment supplier and diistributor Premier Farnell Plc said on Friday it had sold its volume distribution business Farnell Electronic Services (FES) to Arrow Electronics Inc of the U.S. for $300 million cash.
In a statement Premier Farnell said the consideration may be adjusted following a completion audit of FES' net operating assets.
The British company said in a statement it estimated that the disposal would enhance shareholders' funds "by generating a surplus above book value of around 70 million stg".
"The proceeds of the disposal will be applied towards repayment of Premier Farnell's US dollar borrowings," the company added.

After disposing of FES, which concentrates on serving industrial and computer industry manufacturers with large volumes of electornic components, Premier Farnell said it would concentrate on high margin catalogue distribution.

Arrow, on the other hand, will continue to develop its leading position in high volume distribution, and, furthermore, the two companies intend to set cross-purchasing agreements to give eachother beneficial product supplies.

The company described the disposal as "a logical step", while on the London Stock Exchange Premier Farnell shares were marked up swiftly by about 15 pence, or just over 2.0 percent, to stand up 16-1/2 p at 701-1/2 p by 1350 GMT.
